elements.content: Master the core scientific vocabulary and collocations for this topic (10 items):

items.definition: the position in which someone holds their body when standing or sitting.
items.example: Good posture improves lung capacity and alertness.

items.definition: the process of making choices, especially important ones.
items.example: Sitting up straight boosts confidence in decision-making.

items.definition: relating to the mental processes of perception and judgment.
items.example: Proper alignment reduces cognitive fatigue during long study sessions.
Maintaining an upright posture signals self-assurance.

items.definition: a temporary state of mind or feeling.
items.example: Slouching is linked to lower mood and fatigue.

items.definition: the state of being watchful and prompt to meet danger or emergency.
arrangement in a straight line or in correct relative positions.
items.example: Spinal alignment supports optimal blood flow to the brain.

items.definition: designed for efficiency and comfort in the working environment.
items.example: Ergonomic chairs encourage healthy daily seating habits.

items.definition: the feeling or belief that one can rely on someone or something.
items.example: Adopting an upright posture instantly increases self-confidence.

items.definition: a system of parts working together in a machine or process.
items.example: The physiological mechanism involves hormone regulation and oxygen intake.

elements.title: Grammar Explanation (Intermediate (B1))
elements.content:
Use may / might + base verb to express scientific possibilities (e.g., Sitting up straight may improve your mood).

elements.title: Key Study Insights & Core Takeaways
elements.text: Researchers conducted in-depth investigations and empirical trials to analyze these phenomena. The findings reveal critical mechanisms that challenge earlier assumptions.
elements.takeaway: Understanding both biological and empirical evidence allows us to draw more grounded conclusions.
